overall_summary: The channel is experiencing a clear performance divergence. Extreme space anomalies and 'bizarre planet' mysteries (e.g., TrES-2b, Burning Ice, and Supersonic Rubies) are driving the highest engagement and views, consistently crossing the 700-1,000+ view threshold. Conversely, repetitive psychology facts and duplicate uploads of 'fake memories' or 'songs stuck in your head' are severely underperforming, often failing to break double-digit views.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' achieved 1,016 views and 36 likes. 'The Planet of Burning Ice' achieved 1,055 views and 8 likes. 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' achieved 721 views and 25 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme, hostile, or physically paradoxical cosmic environments. Frame them with high-contrast visual prompts and sensory-rich titles.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) and 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views) outperformed general science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Use familiar human senses (smell, taste, touch) to explain massive, abstract cosmic phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' yielded only 5, 11, and 53 views respectively. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Cease immediate re-uploading of identical psychology concepts. If revisiting brain science, pivot to high-stakes cognitive mysteries or AI-brain interfaces.

next_video.concept: The Egg-Shaped Planet Being Eaten Alive (WASP-12b)
next_video.opening_direction: Show a hyper-realistic AI rendering of a pitch-black planet being stretched into an egg shape by a massive star, with the hook: 'Right now, a giant star is literally eating this planet alive.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is so close to its sun that it is being stretched by tidal forces, and in just a few million years, it will completely vanish into the star's core.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the highly successful 'extreme planet' formula that generated our peak views (TrES-2b and Burning Ice) while using a strong visual hook (an egg-shaped planet) to maximize retention.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space survival scenario focusing on extreme planetary conditions (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Planet of Liquid Metal?') to bridge the gap between our top-performing space niche and high-retention storytelling.
